premises: Yttrium addition to a refractory high-entropy alloy can lead to in-situ formation of nanoscale Y2O3 precipitates during an oxidizing anneal.
Nanoscale Y2O3 precipitates can be uniformly dispersed within grains and along grain boundaries in a refractory high-entropy alloy matrix.
Uniformly dispersed nanoscale Y2O3 precipitates act as efficient defect sinks for radiation-induced vacancies and interstitials.
These defect sinks reduce void swelling and irradiation-induced hardening.
The presence of these precipitates preserves the intrinsic ductility and strength of the high-entropy alloy.
